title: Data Dictionary API by Observepoint

DateAndTime.description:
Date-time in [RFC3339 profile ISO 8601 format](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt) with
the following additional restrictions:
1. An uppercase T must separate the date and time portions.
2. An uppercase Z must denote that a numeric time zone offset isn't present.

In general, these timestamp requirements are the same in
[AWS Step Functions - Choice Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/amazon-states-language-choice-state.html)

DataDictionary_SourceEnum.description: Whether the field or definition is managed by ObservePoint or created by the customer

DataDictionary_FieldsDTO.description:
All fields available in a dictionary, both ObservePoint and custom.

Fields returned in the `visibleFields` array are the only fields visible in the specified dictionary,
ordered according to configuration, and enriched with account-specific configuration properties
(e.g. `showInDataPreview`).

The response is narrowed for visitors and for accounts with limited Data Dictionary access.
Those callers get only the subset of visible fields that are flagged `showInDataPreview`, and an
empty `hiddenFields` — a populated hidden list would itself disclose that further fields exist.
Both arrays are always present.

visibleFields.description: Fields visible in this dictionary, in display order. Restricted callers (see the schema description) receive only the fields flagged `showInDataPreview`.

hiddenFields.description: Fields hidden in this dictionary. Always empty for restricted callers (see the schema description), which is not the same as there being no hidden fields.

canEdit.description: Properties of this field that the current user is allowed to update

canDelete.description: Whether the current user is allowed to delete this field

DataDictionary_FieldTrait.description: Common field properties shared across field representations

DataDictionary_FieldFormatEnum.description:
Data format of the field's value:
* `text` - plain text string
* `integer_number` - whole number
* `decimal_number` - decimal number
* `markdown` - markdown-formatted text
* `email` - string, a valid email address, at most 320 characters
* `url` - string, a valid http/https URL, at most 2000 characters
* `duration_seconds` - non-negative whole number of seconds
* `date` - strict ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` string
* `datetime` - ISO-8601 string with a UTC or numeric offset
* `enum` - item id from the field's item catalog (see `DataDictionary_EnumFieldFormatSchema`)
* `entity_reference` - id of a referenced entity (see `DataDictionary_EntityReferenceFieldFormatSchema`)

DataDictionary_FieldFormatSchema.description: Describes the data format of a field's value

isList.description: Whether the field holds a list of values

DataDictionary_EnumItem.description:
One selectable item of an `enum` field. Item ids are client-assigned and stable:
renaming an item keeps its id, so stored definition values are never affected.

id.description:
Client-assigned item id: a non-negative integer (zero allowed),
unique within the field. An id that matches an existing item of the field
renames that item; a new id adds a new item.

value.description: Display value (label) of the item. Unique within the field, case-insensitive.

DataDictionary_EnumFieldFormatSchema.description:
Field format schema for `enum` values. The definition value is an item id
(or an array of item ids when `isList` is `true`).

For custom fields, items can be renamed and new items added; items cannot be removed.
When updating, submit the field's FULL item catalog (like other editable properties,
`enumItems` is replaced as a whole): every existing item id must be present, or the
request is rejected as an attempted removal.

enumItems.description: The selectable items of this field

DataDictionary_ReferencedEntityTypeEnum.description: Which kind of entity an `entity_reference` field's value ids point to

DataDictionary_EntityReferenceFieldForma.description:
Field format schema for `entity_reference` values. The definition value is a positive
integer id of the referenced entity (or an array of ids when `isList` is `true`).
Referenced ids are not existence-checked.

`isList: true` is only supported for `tag` referencedEntityType.

DataDictionary_DisplayMetadata.description: Free-form display metadata for the field (used by the UI)

DataDictionary_DictionarySettings.description: Account-specific configuration for a field within a dictionary

showInDataPreview.description: Whether the field is shown in the definition details preview

DataDictionary_FieldEditablePropertyEnum.description:
A field property that can be updated.
Property names are in camel case, e.g. `display_metadata` enum value corresponds to the `displayMetadata` property.

`format_schema` is advertised for all custom fields, but only `enum` fields have mutable
content: their `enumItems` can be renamed and new items added (never removed).
The `type` and `isList` properties are always immutable, and format schema changes on any
other format are rejected.

DataDictionary_GlobalStatusEnum.description:
Global visibility status of an ObservePoint field.
When `hidden`, users won't be able to see the field at all.

DataDictionary_FieldsUpdateRequestDTO.description:
Full update of all fields, both ObservePoint and custom.
- To create a new field, do not specify an `id`.
- To update a field, specify its `id` and all of its editable properties.
- To reorder fields, change their position in the array.
- To hide a field, move it to the `hiddenFields` array.
- To delete a field, omit it from the request body.

The `canEdit` property (provided by "get fields" endpoint) defines which properties can be updated.
Similarly, `canDelete` defines which fields can be deleted.

Note that fields are shared between dictionaries. Changing a field's name in one dictionary
will also change it in other dictionaries.

visibleFields.description: Fields to be visible in this dictionary, in the desired display order

hiddenFields.description: Fields to be hidden in this dictionary

DataDictionary_FieldUpdate.description:
A field in an update request. Omit `id` to create a new field.
Allowed properties depend on the field source (ObservePoint or custom),
`canEdit` property, and whether this is a create or update operation.
More details in the `DataDictionary_FieldsUpdateRequestDTO` description.

updatedIds.description:
IDs of the fields that actually changed as a result of this request — either their
account settings (visibility, data-preview flag, or position) or an editable property
(name, description, display metadata, enum items).

DataDictionary_OpFieldsDTO.description:
ObservePoint fields with their global default settings. Similar to the regular fields response,
but returns only the ObservePoint default settings, which are not tied to any account.

Note that putting an ObservePoint field in `hiddenFields` will NOT hide it globally,
it will still be visible under "Hidden fields" in the layout editor.
To hide an ObservePoint field globally, update its `globalStatus`.

visibleFields.description: Fields visible in this dictionary by default, in display order

hiddenFields.description: Fields hidden in this dictionary by default

spreadsheetKey.description:
Identifier of the field in the cookie dictionary spreadsheet. Always present for
ObservePoint fields and unique across them; supplied when the field is created and
immutable thereafter.

DataDictionary_OpFieldsUpdateRequestDTO.description:
Update of ObservePoint fields and their global default settings (not tied to any account).
Behaves similarly to the regular fields update, but only allows updating ObservePoint fields.

This is a full-state update of the ObservePoint field catalog, which is shared across all
entity types. An ObservePoint field omitted from the request is deleted globally — not just
for the `{entityType}` in the path — so every request must carry the complete set of
ObservePoint fields.

To prevent accidental data loss, an ObservePoint field cannot be deleted if it has values in customer definitions.
In that case, hide the field instead by setting `globalStatus` to `hidden`.

visibleFields.description: ObservePoint fields to set as visible, in the desired display order

hiddenFields.description: ObservePoint fields to set as hidden

DataDictionary_OpFieldUpdate.description:
Similar to the regular `DataDictionary_FieldUpdate`,
but also includes a `globalStatus` property which controls the global visibility of the ObservePoint field.

Unlike the regular field update, `id` is always required (even when creating a field):
ObservePoint fields use explicit low-numbered ids rather than auto-increment, so the server
determines create vs. update by whether the given `id` already exists.

`spreadsheetKey` is required when creating a new ObservePoint field and must be unique across
all ObservePoint fields. It is ignored when updating an existing field (the key is immutable).

spreadsheetKey.description:
Identifier of the field in the cookie dictionary spreadsheet. Required when creating
a new ObservePoint field; ignored on update.

matchCriteria.description: Rules used to match this definition to the entities. Absent when the current user is not allowed to see match criteria: visitors, and accounts with limited Data Dictionary access.

canEdit.description: Properties of this definition that the current user is allowed to update

canDelete.description: Whether the current user is allowed to delete this definition

operand.description:
Value to match against. The concrete type depends on the property:
a number for `tag_id`, a string for every other property.
String operands are limited to 200 characters.

negated.description: If true, the match criterion is negated

DataDictionary_MatchCriterionPropertyEnu.description: Entity property to match against. Available properties depend on the entity type.

DataDictionary_MatchCriterionOperatorEnu.description: Match operator used to compare the property value against the operand

DataDictionary_DefinitionFieldValue.description: Field's configuration and its value for a definition.

value.description:
Value of the field. The concrete type depends on the field's format:
string for `text`/`markdown`/`email`/`url`/`date`/`datetime`,
number for `integer_number`/`decimal_number`/`duration_seconds`,
an enum item id (number) for `enum`,
a positive integer id of the referenced entity for `entity_reference`.
When the field's `isList` is `true`, the value is an array of the format's scalar type.
May be absent when the field has no value for this definition.

DataDictionary_DefinitionEditablePropert.description:
A definition property that can be updated.
Property names are in camel case, e.g. `match_criteria` enum value corresponds to the `matchCriteria` property.

DataDictionary_DefinitionFieldValueInput.description: A field value to set on a definition

value.description:
Value for the field. The concrete type depends on the field's format:
string for `text`/`markdown`/`email`/`url`/`date`/`datetime`,
number for `integer_number`/`decimal_number`/`duration_seconds`,
an enum item id (number) for `enum`,
a positive integer id of the referenced entity for `entity_reference`.
When the field's `isList` is `true`, the value is an array of the format's scalar type.

DataDictionary_CreateDefinitionRequestDT.description:
Payload to create a custom definition.
`opFieldValues` and `customFieldValues` set field values and are optional.

matchCriteria.description: Rules used to match this definition to the entities

DataDictionary_UpdateDefinitionRequestDT.description:
Payload to update a Data Dictionary definition. The concrete shape is selected by the
`source` discriminator, which must match the definition's actual source; a mismatch is rejected.
- `custom`: see `DataDictionary_UpdateCustomDefinitionRequestDTO`
- `op`: see `DataDictionary_UpdateOpDefinitionRequestDTO`

DataDictionary_UpdateOpDefinitionRequest.description:
Update payload for an ObservePoint-managed definition. Only custom field values may be set;
name, match criteria and ObservePoint field values are not editable for ObservePoint definitions.

DataDictionary_UpdateCustomDefinitionReq.description:
Update payload for a custom definition. `name` and `matchCriteria` are required and are fully
replaced on every update. `opFieldValues` and `customFieldValues` overwrite the respective
field values.

matchCriteria.description: Rules used to match this definition to the entities

DataDictionary_DefinitionFeedbackTrait.description: Feedback properties shared by the submit request and the returned records

DataDictionary_DefinitionFeedbackRequest.description: Feedback submitted for a Data Dictionary definition.

DataDictionary_DefinitionFeedbackListDTO.description: The current user's feedback records for a Data Dictionary definition.

feedback.description: Currently at most one element, the current user's most recent feedback

DataDictionary_DefinitionFeedbackDTO.description: The current user's feedback record; reviewText is absent when no review was given.

DataDictionary_EffectiveDefinitionsDTO.description:
Effective Data Dictionary definitions for the matched entity.
Matching considers contextual properties including page domain, so multiple effective definitions can be returned.

DataDictionary_InContextMatch_EntityProp.description:
Entity properties to match against definition match criteria.
Properties depend on the entity type.

DataDictionary_MatchesRequestDTO.description:
`entityProperties` are the property values to match against definitions (e.g. cookie name, cookie domain, tag ID).

`context` (optional) property is the Audit / Web Journey run ID context for matching.
When provided, it is used to fetch additional details about the entity
(e.g. page domains where a cookie or a tag was observed, tag accounts associated with a tag).
An entity with given `entityProperties` can appear more than once within the context,
so multiple effective definitions can be returned, one for each unique observed variation of an entity in the context.
For example, cookie `_ga (example.com)` may appear on page domains `a.com` and `b.com` in context of a run,
and have separate effective definitions - `_ga (example.com) on a.com` and `_ga (example.com) on b.com`.

`entityProperties` takes precedence over `context`: a property present in `entityProperties`
won't be supplied from the context. But any omitted property (page domain or tag account)
will be supplied from the context if it's provided.

When `context` is not provided, only properties from `entityProperties` are considered for matching.
If some properties are omitted, their respective match criteria won't match.
For example, if `pageDomain` is not provided in `entityProperties`,
definitions that have page domain criteria won't match and won't be returned as effective.

Same as in other places, definition is considered effective if:
1. every match criterion has matched (it's a candidate definition);
2. it is selected among other candidate definitions using tie-breaking algorithm.

When `context` is not provided and some properties are omitted in `entityProperties`,
we may match some definitions partially. Definition is considered a partial match if:
1. it's a custom definition;
2. some of its match criteria has matched, but some has not;
3. every unmatched criterion is unmatched because property value for it was not provided in `entityProperties`.

For example, if there are definitions `tag ID: 1` and `tag ID: 1, tag account: test`,
request has `entityProperties` with `tagId` set to `1`, then the first definition will be effective,
and the second definition will be partially matched.

DataDictionary_MatchesResponseDTO.description:
Effective and partially matched Data Dictionary definitions for the provided entity values.
See more details in `DataDictionary_MatchesRequestDTO` description.

DataDictionary_MatchEntityProperties.description:
Entity properties to match against a definition's match criteria. The properties depend on the entity type.
See more details in `DataDictionary_MatchesRequestDTO` description.

DataDictionary_AuditRunMatchContext.description: Context of an Audit run. `pageId` narrows the context to a single page.

DataDictionary_WebJourneyRunMatchContext.description: Context of a single action in a Web Journey run.
